reviews.text: In the end, The Menu is a little like an unrisen souffle. Delicious but not quite as lofty as it hoped.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: This gourmet show takes unforeseen directions when each step of the menu is transformed into a theatrical act, where the tension will go to a crescendo and the experience that chef Slowik and his team have prepared is not what the diners expected...
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: The Menu is an entertaining horror satire with a marvelous ensemble cast but fails to deliver a slightly interesting punch line.
reviews.author: Arthur Goyaz

reviews.text: “The Menu” demonstrates how capitalism and its relationship to consumerism can actively suck the joy from creatives, particularly as they attempt to fulfil the needs of the most affluent and entitled consumers.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: “The Menu” suggests that such fanatism to an ephemeral art which requires hard work and isolation could lead to a cult like atmosphere brewing insanity and resentment
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: There were so many moments I loved
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: Its A Solid B
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: Despite knowing how the story goes and where the twists and turns are, The Menu is a film that I can see myself going back to again and again.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: The movie captivated the audience in a way that held us hostage to Chef Slowik's emotional manipulation. This was cunningly executed.
reviews.author: Christine Mené

reviews.text: The Menu perfectly and sharply captures the milieu of this fine dining world with a scathing takedown of the condescension and pretension that fuels it.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: Black satire skewers the world of haute cuisine.
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: With splashes of horror and comedy, The Menu explores the world of fine dining restaurants. The movie has a stellar cast, including Fiennes and Taylor-Joy, who are incredible and magnetic together.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: The Menu delivers an engaging time and will leave the audience with a tantalizing sardonic meal.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: ...when the writers found themselves in a difficult plot situation, they resorted to the cheat of some sort of magical powers the Chef can weld with a whisper. Each time such a moment happens, the film begins to lose its grip on the reality of horror.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: The Menu is a perfectly cooked, deliciously evil delight of a film that definitely won't be to everyone's tastes, but if it's your sort of dish at all, you're all but guaranteed to love every minute of it.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: This gastronomic experience leaves no space for its comedic quips or food for thought, leaving way too much to be desired.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: In a unique pairing with the palpable tension comes the dark humor of the film— two facets that usually do not go hand in hand in film as laughter famously diffuses any built up tension, but The Menu cooks up a balance that really works.
reviews.author: Anna Miller

reviews.text: “The Menu” is best explained by Hong Chau’s Elsa when she whispers to one of the guests during dinner: “You’ll eat less than you desire and more than you deserve.”
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: A delicious satire that bites right into any industry that people obsess over. A haunting watch but one that will have you laughing & completely in love with the script.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: The Menu deserves to be seen with very little knowledge of the plot. Even the trailers (and likely this review) give too much away. It’s a dark, vicious satire that expertly unfolds itself over the course of ten dishes.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: A very clean and well-performed movie that lets you get entirely immersed in it with zero distractions from its narrative and its purpose.
reviews.author: Brian Bisesi

reviews.text: stylish and engrossing and sadistically enjoyable
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: The art of the meal and the consumer’s craving for more more s’more are just two of the topics explored in a far tastier “eat the rich” offering than the overcooked Triangle of Sadness.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Never the thought and vision of a cheeseburger made such an impression on me. And by this time your appetite should be big for both the food and the movie.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The story, penned by Will Tracy and Seth Reiss, is expertly paced, punctuated by gorgeous title cards announcing the dishes.
reviews.author: Audra Schroeder

reviews.text: Bad pretentious art that thinks it's critiquing bad pretentious art, told exclusively through the medium of food metaphors? ...yay.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: It’s a slow-building revelation that will result in a gasp, and then it just builds on the “out there” abilities of a thriller/horror hybrid. Come for Ralph Fiennes, but stay for the outrageously bizarre finale.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: As horror-satire goes, The Menu isn’t especially sophisticated. And true foodies can probably poke holes in every course. But in its own insistently odd way, the film is a good deal of palate-cleansing fun.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Finally, we have the definitive proof that American cheese on a burger is good.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: Mark Mylod brings a healthy balance of entertainment and satire to his audience, accented by delicious performances from a cast of characters that make us question what a fine dining experience should look like.
reviews.author: Patrick Hicks

reviews.text: Dark, wry, scathing, and utterly riveting, The Menu serves a deliciously twisted treat.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Both 'Glass Onion' and 'The Menu' owe some of their success and much of our enjoyment to the late, great Lady Mallowan. We are deep into Agatha Christie territory here.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: It's a movie that I was enjoying with each bite as it was going along, because it's not just about culinary obsession...but it's a damning criticism of how we consume art.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: Its critical view of the economic elite is one that Cinema, as a politically dynamic Art, reflects with increasing frequency in a reality in which social inequalities become greater and greater. [Full review in Portuguese]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: .... "The Menu" is a delicious treat from appetizer to dessert, balancing the sweet and savory to offer a unique experience that ultimately reminds audiences not to f*** with the people who serve you.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The Menu starts off intriguing, but eventually gets too bogged down becoming the very thing it’s spoofing.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Mylod has some fun with it, and Fiennes does some delicious work. But its eat the rich allegories are half-baked at best.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Splicing horror and comedy with skill and delight, the movie is a satire of class, privilege, and pretension that's also at its core a supremely entertaining story.
reviews.author: Sam Haysom

reviews.text: ... A genuinely hilarious send-up of everything in the world of art, from those who create to those who consume. While this isn’t unique subject matter, the way that the plot unfolds is.
reviews.author: Sol Harris

reviews.text: Little by little, its plot loses its intriguing effect and ends up becoming a tasteless dish. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: This is a brilliant and intricate understanding of how art is the root of culture, and when there is no other purpose left for it, the artist resorts to self-immolation for the survival of creation.
reviews.author: Konstantina Buhalis

reviews.text: Pretty enjoyable on its own terms, and as long as you don't need it to be too precise in its satiric aims.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A wickedly delicious satire of fine dining obsession.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: Neither fun nor scathing, funny nor insightful, the film coasts on second-rate quips and third-rate violence.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: This sinister, satirical dark comedy is undoubtedly one of the most bizarrely absurd thrillers of the year, skewering pretentious 'foodies' and the 'fine dining' they crave.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Led by Anya Taylor-Joy and Ralph Fiennes, the film explores classism and wealth through the performative lens of food and nostalgia.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: Anya Taylor-Joy anchors a wickedly entertaining satire.
reviews.author: Santanu Das

reviews.text: The "eat the rich" movie of the year.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: A tingling black comedy awash with thrills, wit, and well-earned heartburn. Reaching for the Tums has never been so much fun.
reviews.author: Brandon Judell

reviews.text: A competently prepared dish that would like to be thought of, ultimately, as a well-made cheeseburger.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: The visually intimate and beautiful set, slowly turns into a claustrophobic and horrifying space. This is definitely worth the price of admission! Just remember to tip your waiter.
reviews.author: Kevin Sampson

reviews.text: The Menu is thematically untidy and slightly underdeveloped in spots, rendering it merely good instead of great. Otherwise, it’s a pointedly absurd, consistently funny and suspenseful chamber-piece thriller with strong performances and a sharp edge.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text:
The Menu is an interesting look at class structure, a cultish devotion to art and a deconstruction of pretentiousness in today's society. 

Ralph Fiennes and Anya Taylor-Joy do an incredible job.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: The Menu is just out there, its violent, intentionally creepy, dark, and at times horrifically comedic and I truly loved every minute of it. With a great cast, very interesting concept for the script & devotion to the characters is always felt. A MUST SEE
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: It’s here we begin to see The Menu as a story about class and inequality, which swiftly translates into a reign of terror inflicted by the serfs on their social superiors.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Director Mark Mylod lays on the dark comedy as thick as a creamy garlic aioli in this tasty thriller.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: The very definition of a slow-burn thriller... (like) the soft ticking of a kitchen timer teasing the cooking meal to come, waiting as the air fills with an aroma thick enough to already taste.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: THE MENU is a dark star of a satire with ornate dishes that are full of self-loathing and human frailty. It lovingly catalogs the artist’s attempt to share the contents of their soul with people who understand. THE MENU is refined, precise, and deadly.
reviews.author: Dolores Quintana

reviews.text: Mylod  believes satire is a dish best served cold. But not when it’s this icy. It requires a modicum of warmth. And without it, “The Menu” struggles to pass the taste test. Still, try it, you might like it. But don’t forget the Alka Seltzer.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Even if the film’s social commentary and satirical edge feels like a badly-tossed salad of ideas, its controlled directing, quick pacing, and fantastic performances provide some flavorful textures and cinematic bites.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: The third act proves somewhat rushed and messy, the joke finding its limits with apparently nowhere to go. Thankfully, however, Mylod and company do stick the landing, pivoting back to cold, calculating finality.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The actors make it work—among them, Hong Chau as the devoted maitre’d refusing people bread...
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: The Menu is not what you would call good family fun, but it could be fun to watch this Thanksgiving with a particularly perverse family.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: The Menu could have done with slightly more nuance, but it’s a gripping black comedy that grills its characters to perfection.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Ralph Fiennes and Anya Taylor-Joy are sensational in this punctual satire that surprises us dish after dish, down to the last bite. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The Menu is a well-made and fun horror-satire that smartly dabbles in class, wealth, and criticism, featuring a good, strong cast.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: The film fares better as a tightly constructed exercise in horror, like a cross between the mechanized death of a Saw movie and the eat-the-rich grotesquerie of Peter Greenaway’s The Cook, the Thief, His Wife & Her Lover.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: While it's a tad overlong, I greatly enjoyed this. It was interesting, thought provoking and as an artist, I greatly connected with the motives behind the event.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: I greatly enjoyed this entertaining thriller that wasn't as graphic as I thought it would be. The fact that the actors all bought into the concept and executed at 100% made it even more entertaining.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Clever and creepy, this satire skewers the elite and plays well into other similar films.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: While “The Menu” isn’t as clever as “Knives Out,” it does manage to deflate pretense and show just how equal everyone is in a tense situation. It’s funny, but it’s deadly serious. Don’t go with a full stomach and be sure to try the popcorn.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: As much as I liked it... at the end of the day, it's not quite as smart as it thinks it is.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: A different That Shelf take on Mark Mylod’s THE MENU, an edgy black comedy that elevates the angry satire and tickles the audience in a hilariously ingenious way.
reviews.author: Tamara Khodova

reviews.text: The Menu is simultaneously as understated as a pinch of salt and as subtle as a ghost pepper. This is a black comedy wearing the guise of a horror movie or a thriller, and it is better when it embraces the comedy elements.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Confusing plot elevated by superb acting all way round.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The comedy elements run toward heavy-handed absurdity, and the thrills are telegraphed too early and often.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: An over seasoned satirical thriller from producers Adam McKay and Will Ferrell bites off a little more than it can chew.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: The Menu is an atmospheric, claustrophobic thriller with a killer ending, but manages to fall short in serving up a full-course of deranged delights.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The satire may be delivered with the subtlety of a rolling pin, but The Menu is never less than entertaining thanks to sizzling performances from a steely-eyed Fiennes, sycophantic Hoult and sleazy Leguizamo.
reviews.author: Max Copeman

reviews.text: …exactly the blast of populist, adult orientated entertainment that the big screen has been sorely lacking of late…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: A top-notch exploration of the toxic relationship between art, artist and consumer. Sharp satire, commentary with precise cuts, and tantalizing tension that brings the heat.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: A black comedy that perhaps could have been a little more ambitious -or less obvious in its ambitions-, but like any good plate of food, can be enjoyed without problems. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Slowik’s slow-cooked revenge against social inequality, bad taste, cruel critique, culinary pretension and even ‘fast food’ cinema is unsettling and accusatory.
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: From amuse bouch to dessert, this thriller earns its stripes in satirizing pretensions.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: As with food, sometimes simple is best and with the right ingredients, you can serve up a sumptuous dish - The Menu is a deliciously dark comedy with some devilish horror beats thrown in for good measure, it's a real treat.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Some may quibble with the film's direct approach, but what The Menu lacks in subtlety it more than makes up for with scathing satire and a trio of exceptional performances from Fiennes, Taylor-Joy and Chau.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: It’s easy to point and laugh at the rich, or feel a sense of vindication... But you still walk away feeling hungry.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: A delightfully despicable B-horror comedy disguised as an artsy meditation on creation and commerce.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: A savage, savvy and scathingly amusing satire about coveting $1250-a-head meals but letting the workers behind them slice, steam, stir and sweat through upscale kitchen drudgery.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Stylishly photographed by Peter Deming, The Menu becomes increasingly creepy with each new course.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: I think it all gets squandered by trying to shovel it into satire.
reviews.author: Leila Latif

reviews.text: I don't think I necessarily felt satisfied by the climax of this film, but it's a very stylish affair. I very much enjoyed being in the world it's set in. It left me hungry for more, I guess.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Like the appetizers, entrees, and apertifs so lovingly filmed here, The Menu is a fetish object styled as an indulgent antidote to unearned pretension, one meant to be appreciated, not to be enjoyed.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: With limited depth, but effervescent. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: An intelligent dilemma that portents to be more scandalous than what it actually serves; The Menu is an agile ode to the inherent beauty of a pretentious dish while simultaneously questioning its existence. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: The marvelous, multitalented Ralph Fiennes is the best thing on the menu in this clever culinary delight.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Anya Taylor-Joy and Nicholas Hoult prove to be more irresistible together than apart... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Rosado

reviews.text: ...a slow-burn endeavor that admittedly (and effectively) captures the viewer’s interest right from the get-go...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The Menu is a twisted horror film that’s a delectable experience and keeps you on the edge of your seat.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: In a continuing series of 2022 films destroying the rich this clever, cheeky horror-comedy is a real delight. The only thing difficult in recommending it is trying to avoid the cliched food adjectives to describe it. All of which apply.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: While the movie can lack believability and doesn’t always push things as far as it could, this is an exquisitely crafted film with a sense of humor that lingers throughout the entire movie
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: I feel like if you like a good thriller... you'll enjoy yourself, but if you're you're a foodie who likes fine cuisine and also you happen to like a thriller, this movie was made for you.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: There’s no romantic spark between Fiennes and Taylor-Joy. There’s something better. Both actors have unfettered access to their inner villains.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Edalatpour

reviews.text: The Menu serves up a ghoulish and madly entertaining two hours of prime cinema.
reviews.author: Gerald Peary

reviews.text: Foodie culture is slayed, literally, in this expert black comedy.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Entertaining and slight. It's an amuse-bouche, not the whole meal.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: It looked and felt and seemed a lot better than it really is.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: Mark Mylod has shown a talent for skewering the wealthy and the pretentious on Succession, and this is a more obvious flambeing and with tongue planted much more firmly in the cheek.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: A delectable cinematic treat, one that’s consistently smart, funny and engaging.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Mylod balances the tones without allowing the pacing to lag. When it’s funny, it’s really funny. When it’s tense, it almost veers into horror territory.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: The Menu is twisty, turny, funny, a little bit demented, and, even with high expectations, more satisfying than expected. It is, as they say, the whole enchilada.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: As raw and sharp as the situation deserves.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Santiago Alverú

reviews.text: Between Fiennes and Taylor Joy a most exquisite duel takes place that lasts 108 minutes without failing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The film is exactly what it wants to be and is unafraid to prove that it's unique, different, refreshing, searing, and above all, destined to entertain an adult audience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: Unfortunately, there’s really nothing mysterious here other than motive, and once that’s revealed, The Menu collapses.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: The Menu serves up a lot of expected jokes and twists, but does so in a fun and engaging package.
reviews.author: Christopher James

reviews.text: An unsubtle, but nonetheless hilarious satire of foodie culture, featuring strong performances from Fiennes, Taylor-Joy and Chau. This may be too obvious for some, but the comedy, particularly the description of dishes and the smores finale, is divine
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: The Menu is a masterfully dark comedy severed extra vicious and deviously delicious.
reviews.author: Mark McPherson

reviews.text: Strong performances and deadpan humour ensure this dark comedy is brought to the boil.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: If you are in the mood of a darkly black comedy and an amusing foodie movie “The Menu” should suit the menu.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: “The Menu” is part psychological thriller and part horror movie. There will be blood. There are moments that are wickedly funny. After watching the unique, fast-paced, and savory film, you may never eat S’mores again.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: A movie that will devour your attention from start to finish.
reviews.author: Alex Barr

reviews.text: A scary chef (Ralph Fiennes) catering only to the filthy rich leaves room for a lot of explaining to do about how he treats his regulars.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: an enticing dish, elegant yet hearty, with a delectable mélange of satire, dark comedy, and horror, to be savored by foodies and anti-foodies alike
reviews.author: Ayelet Dekel

reviews.text: Seems over-stuffed and half-baked...We end up with an affair that is as pretentious as the culinary culture it strives to spoof. Still, you’ve got to hand it to Ralph Fiennes, whose performance deserved to be the centrepiece of a much better film.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Bolstered by Seth Reiss and Will Tracy’s engrossingly clever script, Mark Mylod’s The Menu is an intense game of wits bursting with flavor that thrills, delights, and excites.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: What makes The Menu feel less like a traditional horror is a stellar cast of Fiennes, Taylor-Joy, and Light, along with the biting satire that floats as dry as a leaf in autumn. It’s darkly funny even when you’re gasping as you’re giggling.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: No cow is sacred when fine dining takes a nosedive.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: 'The Menu' is a smorgasbord of surprises!  Chances are you'll gladly pick up this cinematic check and add a generous tip to boot.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: A film that is both dark and funny, “The Menu” benefits from the combination of a smartly written script and some excellent performances.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Marketed as an upscale spin on horror, The Menu interrogates a culture that has taken the chef from faceless grunt to something of a cult leader.
reviews.author: Alison Herman

reviews.text: A delicious social satire about consumer culture in which no one comes out unscathed, from pretentious critics, FOMO addicts, & obsessive fandom, using food as a metaphor, with dark humor as the main ingredient. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: The Menu is shocking, gripping, and full of jaw-dropping moments. Food fans will get their fill, and anyone who loves an intense thriller will have an excellent time with this one.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: There’s just so much to love about “The Menu”: its sparkling cast, its gonzo premise, its gripping storytelling, and Mark Mylod’s pinpoint direction (and that’s just for starters).
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Ralph Fiennes proves no one can best him when it comes to playing villainous characters, delivering a delicious performance we won't soon forget.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: This movie isn’t for everyone. It’s intense, unforgiving, and pulls no punches. The filmmakers attack the anti-hoi polloi here with the precision of a brain surgeon’s scalpel and show no quarter in the process.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: A film that owns its pretentiousness and is best served to patrons unaware of what they’re about to ingest, The Menu is a dark, twisted delight enhanced by the first-class sparring between Fiennes and Taylor-Joy.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: The line between serf and nobleman slowly disappears with the delivery of each course to a guest’s table, which only augments how dazzlingly unhinged this madness proves to be.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Mark Mylod's satirical horror puts a clever spin on the "eat the rich" anecdote that, while mesmerizing to look at, leaves us hungry for more.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: A study in austere modernism, restaurant Hawthorne isn't just a place to eat, it's the physical embodiment of rarified consumer aspiration...
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A black comedy that skewers the capitalist class divide through the prism of pretentious haute cuisine....has some succulent ingredients but in the end, like so many haute cuisine servings, it leaves you hungry for something more substantial.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: The disappointing ending falls short of the devilish deliciousness that comes before, but "The Menu" is a wickedly savage, genre-blending thriller that provides arthouse fun for foodies.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: This beautiful dish of a movie is refreshing, smart, and fun and best served in this dark comedy thriller fashion.
reviews.author: Joshua Mackey

reviews.text: Perhaps the highest compliment I can offer The Menu is simply that I haven’t been able to stop thinking about it. The film is as well executed and as emotionally distant as the very food it depicts.
reviews.author: Tori Preston

reviews.text: The Menu is food that looks better as a social media post than an actual meal with a surprising lack of follow-through and purpose when one peels back even the initial layer of what the film presents.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Ultimately, The Menu isn’t telling us anything we don’t already know. The digs are surface level, the characterisations somewhat heavy-handed, but the script is sharp and darkly funny enough to get away with it.
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: A half-baked breadstick posing as haute cuisine, this movie is neither filling, nor as slyly sophisticated as it pretends to be.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Even inattentive viewers will find themselves pretty far ahead of the film before we get to the just desserts.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: From amuse-bouche to the most epic dessert, Mark Mylod’s The Menu delivers a feast that increases in both heat and flavor as the film descends into chaos. It’s both a savory ode to the culinary world and a spicy takedown of the rich.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: It may be snarky, but “The Menu” is also elegantly entertaining.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: This is a full-bodied swipe at foodie culture from top to bottom. If you're worried you might miss the joke, don't worry - chances are you know more about food than you think.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Darkly, deliciously humorous and razor-sharp in its class commentary.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: The satire hits the high marks for originality, creativity, dark humor and horror factor.  A crafty feast for the eyes and devilishly delectable.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Ralph Fiennes delivers one of the most memorable characters of the year in this solid culinary dark comedy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Fiennes and Taylor-Joy have some scenes together that are among the year's best.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: An exciting, tension-filled odyssey that leaves audiences unsettled by its delicious mix of horror and pitch black humor
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: It’s pretty easy to see how the pinnacle of fine dining for the super-rich, or those that will aspirationally break the bank for one night at the table, can be spun into a satire so sharp it could cut sashimi from twenty paces.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: The Menu has all the right ingredients for a cutting black comedy. It is deliciously funny eat-the-rich cinema.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: The Menu invites us not to mindlessly consume, but to savor all it has to offer.
reviews.author: Cass Clarke

reviews.text: The key flavour is black comedy but he also cooks up mystery and suspense with a soupçon of pulpy horror.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Subtle it’s not, but it’s maliciously entertaining. It turns out that revenge on the ultra-wealthy is a dish best seared over a naked flame.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: It’s ultimately about things that almost everyone will relate to, both intellectually and viscerally.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: A frothy mixture of dark comedy, thrills, and ultimately horror that goes down as smoothly as strawberry puree. Director Mark Mylod has taken this concoction and whisked it into a mile-high soufflé.
reviews.author: Neely Swanson

reviews.text: Mark Mylod’s dark comedy serves up Tales from the Crypt vibes as the spotlight shifts from the food to the guests leaving the audience appreciating the value of ordering delivery. Anya Taylor-Joy and Ralph Fiennes make great antagonists.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: The delectable storytelling helps The Menu become one of the most entertaining films of 2022, one that is sure to only grow with repeat viewings.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: The Menu is mostly empty fun; not profound or clever enough to be truly memorable, but constantly a good time and ripe for rewatches.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: This modern foodie take on the well-traveled “The Most Dangerous Game” narrative manages to skirt the formula while touching on impactful themes.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The next time you're hungry, it just might have you opting for the drive-thru.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Initially, the target of the satire being served up by British director Mark Mylod... appears to be the fussy pretensions of high-end fine dining... Behind the comedy, however, something darker is going on.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: The archetypes never rise above their easy-target personalities, & that is the main problem. It lacks a theme or centerpiece, except to point there are Weird foodies! Vain movie stars! Wealthy people without morality!  Which is what everyone already knows
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Credit the film for audacity, although the social commentary becomes muddled, with a rather aimless takedown of wealth and capitalist privilege that doesn’t give us much to chew on.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Unpredictable and visceral, this is the menu; a wild dark satire, in which extravagance and suspense are the main course to taste. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aldo Javier Martínez

reviews.text: I've had better meals but The Menu still provides plenty of great performances, an intriguing premise and some beautiful food porn. Plus, we critics get to butcher food puns in our reviews, which is always a welcome treat.
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text: ... An intelligent and unpredictable exercise in suspense. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: It's complete nonsense, but this very dark horror-comedy strikes just the right notes of stone-cold humor and red-hot malevolence, making for a delectable dish that satisfies all the way down.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: This is a horror movie. It's funny, twisted and its got an insidious undertone that works as it becomes increasingly unhinged
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: Send this Menu back to the kitchen.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: The dialogue is disappointing, the plotting inconsistent and it’s hard to care about any of the characters. If you want culinary drama, Boiling Point and The Bear are far more interesting.
reviews.author: Markie Robson-Scott

reviews.text: The Menu slows down a bit after a point and becomes drab but picks itself up quickly. The film will especially appeal to fans of all things cynical. The sinuous vein will spook you out!
reviews.author: Dhaval Roy

reviews.text: Black comedy, conformity and death blend in a sumptuous cinematic stew...
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: From the first scene to the final cut to black, I was enthralled by the unique, unpredictable story.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Fiennes’ comic touch is delightful, and the scenes he shares with Taylor-Joy’s tough and wily Margot are electrifying.​
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: A shiny but blunt-edged culinary satire.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Maybe the film wants to challenge that us versus them binary dynamic and suggest it is useless. But much of the film is built on that notion and when it's taken down it does not offer anything in its place.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: To ding this for not completely sticking the landing -- from going from fulfilling to simply filling -- is to ignore so much of what this straight-outta-Jacobean-theatre chamber piece does right.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: More food for thought than your average glossy fall thriller tends to offer.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: If the film’s raison d’etre is to show up the vapidity of modern art, then it produces no argument better than itself. Dumb but delicious, The Menu is a feast for the senses, if not the brain.
reviews.author: Nick Hilton

reviews.text: The Menu is a full meal, covering every inch of the plate with fierce commentary, and taking sharp bites about the society we all live in.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: The Willy Wonka storyline is aped here, as one naughty guest after another faces up to their fate in a thinly disguised morality play.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Like a dumber, drunken Midsommar, instead of insights into trauma/romantic vs communal love, it stumbles and slurs its words, yelling “No, you know what? You’re ALL jerks!” It’s not wrong… It’s fun to hear sloppy rants about obvious injustices sometimes.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Savagely satirical of wealthy, submissive diners who respond to cruelty like frightened birds. It's tight, well written and loaded with excellent performances - like the subtle depth charge of wordless Judith Light.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: The Menu is a deliciously diabolical and delectably dark feast, and the less you know going into it, the better served you are.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: The Menu's satire is as sharp as the knives in its celebrity chef's kitchen, savagely funny from start to finish and a master class in pitch black comedy.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: It’s got a delicious mean streak and enough satirical flavor to play its relative shagginess to its advantage.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: For much of the film's runtime, it is immensely enjoyable. [...] But when "The Menu" sets out to give itself meaning, to be more than an alternatingly funny and upsetting horror-comedy, it struggles to find its footing.
reviews.author: Derek Deskins

reviews.text: Despite a mildly disappointing course or two, The Menu is a movie well worth tasting and savoring, if not considering all that seriously.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Mylod’s stew saves its most mouth-watering plate for the last. That’s why it’s fiendishly delightful.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Deliciously wicked, Mark Mylod’s “The Menu” gleefully skewers elitism in all its forms, laying waste to the pretentious and privileged with abandon...one thing’s for sure – after watching it, you’ll never look at S’mores in the same way again.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: There is much to chew on from this menu. You’ll be drooling at the food, wary of the company, and psyched out by the Chef of this exclusive restaurant who serves up a dangerously intimidating meal.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: If the price for exquisiteness, political correctness, and social appearances is usually sacrificed, The Menu takes this requisite to extreme situations to hilarious and delirious effect. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: Like Triangle of Sadness but with a pulpier sensibility, The Menu purports to be a takedown of the overconsumption habits of the super-rich.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: As a cinematic experience, The Menu is akin to what Hawthorn passes off as grande cuisine and high-level gastronomy. It looks impressive but tastes dull.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: Taylor-Joy, always compelling, is radiant here.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: A delectable dish of revenge, which is a dish best served cold. With this ensemble cast, Mylod has all the right ingredients to create a memorable experience. Once you’ve had your fill, there’s no chance that you’ll be asking for s’more.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: The Menu is not an easy watch potentially churning your stomach at the sheer lengths it goes to, some of which may have you laughing out of discomfort. It’s wildly unpredictable, and yet, oddly familiar.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: It's set up like an Agatha Christie mystery, but also has the trappings horror -- blood is shed, and not only by luckless livestock.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: As if run through a Paco Jet, Ralph Fiennes delivers an icy tour-de-force as a mesmerizing, disturbed chef at the end of his rope.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: You may not be completely satisfied, but you'll still have fun while consuming it.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: Foodie culture gets hilariously torched as a celebrity chef, acted to pretentious perfection by Ralph Fiennes, holds his customers, except for a deliciously defiant Anya Taylor-Joy, to the fire at his restaurant from hell. It’s all delectably unhinged.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: A pitch-black meditation on the confluence of power, wealth, and taste.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: What makes The Menu more satiating than other recent, glitzier skewerings of ultracapitalism is that its satire isn’t so glib that it leaves you feeling comfortably outside of the proceedings.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Fiennes’ performance is key to The Menu’s overall effect. He plays Julian like a cross between Primo, Stanley Tucci’s chef character from Big Night who values purity above all else, and Hannibal Lecter.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Hoult, Fiennes and ­Taylor-Joy are brilliant, but The Menu suffers from a heavy helping of self-satisfaction.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: The Menu is enormous fun throughout, and as you might expect of a cast led by Ralph Fiennes and Anya Taylor-Joy, gloriously acted.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Part “Seven,” part haute-cuisine “Saw,” part reality cooking show, director Mylod’s film finally isn’t sure of how far to push the effrontery. It helps, however, to have Fiennes in the kitchen and a Nordic smokehouse out back.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: “The Menu” might make you crave a hamburger or think twice before boarding a ferry to a private island with no cell service. But once the loose ends are tied up and the credits roll, it leaves you less than satisfied.
reviews.author: Joy Ashford

reviews.text: Bizarre, original and loaded with revelatory surprises with every turn of the page, The Menu uses the culture of haute cuisine as a metaphor for the spit-roasted values of high society, with results that are vicious, delicious, and horrifying.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Its sheer willingness to bite the hand that feeds this world will be irresistible to those with a taste for what’s being served.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: This is an examination of wealth and privilege, where people are so out of touch with everyday life that they’ve become caricatures without even realizing it.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: As The Menu unfolds with the sharpness of a steak knife, it’s hard to predict what deranged delights it will serve up next. It's a sumptuous multi-course meal that never feels overstuffed. The dishes are divinely shot, the humour deliciously dry.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: While THE MENU is certainly provocative --- and electrifying --- it is Fiennes’ performance that keeps the audience spellbound.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: THE MENU is one of those completely original ideas that will sneak up on unsuspecting viewers. The movie drips with anticipation of what will occur next.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: A sumptuously crafted thriller that sports a great cast, sharp writing, and a fun story if you have the appetite for it.
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: a tightly wound, sharply rendered skewering of the dichotomy between the takers and the givers, or in this case, the eaters and the cooks.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: The dish being served here is perhaps too spicy for most. If you like your comedy as black as squid ink, however, there is a lot to savor on this menu.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Fiennes is perfectly cast as the moody, pompous, celebrity chef who creates masterpieces.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: The Menu shows its hand early and leaves viewers salivating for a subversion of expectations, a la David Fincher's The Game, that never arrives.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The movie offers a serving of social commentary as it skewers the one percent.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Horror-comedies like this are a tough thing to get right, but once The Menu really gets going, the laughs come just as frequently as the thrills.
reviews.author: Eric Langberg

reviews.text: A cast fronted by A-listers, a richly detailed set and a dedication to culinary authenticity do not save this work from a story that aims high but falls short.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: If you love a little horror mixed into your black comedy (or vice-versa), then this is one in-cinema experience you won’t want to miss.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: The casting and framing of The Menu is rich, flavorful and brilliant. The plot, however, is gruel-thin.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Leading a well-cast ensemble, Ralph Fiennes plays a mad genius.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Shot beautifully, scripted perfectly and acted wonderfully, The Menu is a dark comedy/horror in the tradition of 1995’s The Last Supper that uses a clever setup to explore real characters in an unreal situation.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: When interest begins to wane, everything is left in the magnificent hands of Fiennes and Taylor-Joy, the only ones who stay above the sea of over-the-top impostures and an initially irresistible menu that turns bland... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: Not even Ralph Fiennes, Anya Taylor-Joy, and Nicholas Hoult can make the flavors in Mark Mylod’s latest film work together.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Despite appearances, the film’s desire to unsettle runs a distant second to its desire to please. Bearing that in mind, The Menu offers a fair amount of holiday fun.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Soup to nuts, The Menu is satisfying and rich, yet lean and cutting.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: The Menu is a harsh commentary that might be too on-the-nose at times, but the characters created by Fiennes and Taylor-Joy are riveting and a joy to watch.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: The Menu is the most fun anyone can have at the movies this year that involves becoming hungry, laughing heartily, and being revolted all at the same time.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: The Menu is a win. Fiennes, Hoult, and Taylor-Joy elevate every scene that they are in, and take the ones they share to incredible heights. Mylod crafts a knife-cuttingly suspenseful tale that is ultimately worth the theatrical experience.
reviews.author: Liam Crowley

reviews.text: Satire of the darkest possible, hilarious kind, best served with plenty of popcorn.
reviews.author: Bethany Jean Clement

reviews.text: A dark comic thriller of rare and mouthwatering fiendishness, in which every scene adds kick and savour to the next.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: The Menu is most convincing in its first hour when secrets are still being cooked. The last act, whatever was been brewing in that chic seaside restaurant with bullet-proof windows, loses steam. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Ralph Fiennes knows exactly what movie he’s in: a bleak comedy where he’s simultaneously the audience’s arbiter of vengeance against the worst of the 1% and also the clear-cut villain.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Ralph Fiennes and Anya Taylor-Joy star in this dark comedy that serves up a few shocking surprises.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: The Menu is an incredibly nuanced film with layer after layer in its fantastical feast, and depending on the viewer, you stop and focus on a particular course.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: [The Menu] may be aimed at somewhat low-hanging fruit and may ultimately not have all that much to chew on. But [directed Mark Mylod] brings an icy, stylish flare in another kind of cleverly staged eat-the-rich comedy that is still a very tasty snack.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: It doesn’t land perfectly at the end but overall it’s a hoot if you have the stomach for it.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: A little more depth to the bitter flavour might not have gone amiss, but ultimately this is a near perfectly executed meal of a movie, made with exceptional ingredients and skill.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: An admirably wicked and angry comedy, The Menu offers little mercy in its twisted game of culture war and class struggle.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Moviegoers known to spend hours watching the Food Network or steeped in celebrity chef worship may appreciate the milieu, which plays as though torture porn had been introduced into The Trip series.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Menu offers up a choice selection of social critique and biting humor, so be sure to come hungry.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The film’s secret weapon though is Chau, whose barely masked condescension epitomizes the relationship between her chef and those circumstance has forced him to serve.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: “Eat the rich” might be a popular theme this movie season, but “The Menu” takes the idea to extremes that finally overpower the palate.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Its appetite for destruction is... too much fun in the end to refuse: a giddy little amuse bouche for the apocalypse to come.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: There is nothing subtle about “The Menu,” but that’s a large part of its charm.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: Perhaps the thing that makes The Menu so delicious is the taste that accompanies watching the ultra-rich get trussed up and stuffed like Thanksgiving turkeys.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: It’s as subtle as fermented Surströmming (look it up) but this mix of horror and humor has more to offer than shock value. Food for thought on how art is consumed (literally in this case), it’s about artist's passions and what happens when it fades.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Mark Mylod skewers wealthy elitists in a deliciously funny black comedy. The Menu serves up sweet revenge on a cinematic platter. The beck and call working class that caters to foolish affluent whims should be first in line to see this film.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: The Menu succumbs to horror stereotypes in the last 15 minutes of the film. However, the overall movie is an entertaining ride that pokes fun at pretentiousness and obsessive ambition that are spawned from the pursuit of fame, wealth, and power.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The Menu not only has all the right ingredients — from the cast to the ominous cinematography and a wicked screenplay – but manages to deliver even more than what is promised.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: The satisfaction one can get from watching a film that carefully and intelligently tears down, tears open, and skewers rich people is incomparable. Mark Mylod's The Menu is a sly, extra sharp satire that isn't afraid of offering us some dry-aged humor...
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: Horribly cynical, conceptually overwrought, leaves a very bad taste. Shall not be returning.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: An eat-the-rich satire that would go rotten without its supremely overqualified cast, The Menu is as much fun as it is ephemeral.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: A savory dark comedy that brilliantly skewers obsessive food culture.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: I enjoyed the unpredictability, having the film give me a sigh of relief through a laugh that was much needed at that time.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Fiennes sneakily delivers one of the best comedic performances of the year without resorting to one-liners and big energy.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Foodies, celebrity chefs, the filthy rich—this is low-hanging fruit for a satirist. But The Menu dices each with Ginsu precision.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: The Menu does well at subverting expectations when pertaining to the characters we experience throughout the story.
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: Have you ever watched an episode of Netflix’s Chef’s Table and thought, “gee, I wish this was more like a horror movie.” Well, I present to you weirdos The Menu
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: The Menu puts the super-rich on the chopping block in an island setting for a little eat-the-rich-style payback.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: It is well-acted and well directed by Mylod with tasty side plates of droll humour.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The satire is actually what I liked most about the movie. There’s plenty of truth to the various avatars who represent a diner. The tech bros or VC types are almost as cartoonishly ridiculous as the movie depicts.
reviews.author: Cesar Hernandez

reviews.text: It’s maybe not one of the best movies of 2022, but it was certainly one of my favorites.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A deliciously twisted and darkly funny takedown of the rich and high-class food world. The ending is an all-timer, offering inventively disturbing, playfully evil imagery that will have one salivating in admiration
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The film mutates as time passes to something more satirical, uncomfortable, and ultimately horrific, reaching disturbing sadistic levels. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: An exquisite game of reveals that leads to a satisfying, and beautifully theatrical, resolution.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: A razor sharp comedy about the inevitability of the artist hating his patrons. Perfectly realized, every joke lands, and Hong Chau is incredible.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: While Anya Taylor-Joy gives a solid performance as Margot, it really is Fiennes’ movie. "The Menu" is a wickedly dark comedy that uses satire to take on elitism in the world of luxury dining.
reviews.author: Chauncey K. Robinson

reviews.text: The Menu’s straight-faced depiction of absurd culinary violence may not be imaginative or thrilling, but the film is rarely boring. It’s deep-fried junk disguised as gastronomy; it may not fully satisfy, but it’ll fill a hole.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The Menu serves up a taut laugh riot and a successful takedown of the fine-dining industry and its ego.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: My favorite film of the 2022 Toronto International Film Festival.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: It's a vintage ensemble who, had they been given meatier topics to deal with, could have delivered an all-timer. As it is though, The Menu is a darkly funny, often shocking and unique black comedy that constantly keeps you on edge.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: A captivating thriller that will have audiences on the edge of their seat as everything unfolds — and really craving a cheeseburger. Leads Anya Taylor-Joy and Nicholas Hoult bring their A-game.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Mylod, working from a script by Seth Reiss and Will Tracy, goes all in on the social commentary. Some of it is funny, some of it appalling, none of it as engaging as when Mylod uses food to make statements.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: … a sharp, acidic offering with an occasionally bitter taste, but enough of a pleasant mouthfeel to have audiences licking their plates and asking for seconds.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: For as potent as the film’s shocks can be in the moment, it’s difficult to shake off that the screenplay lacks for the breadth of variety that’s necessary to make more than just a restaurant’s tasting menu take flight.
reviews.author: Wes Greene

reviews.text: Despite my not loving the ending the script for The Menu is very well done and it builds tension exceptionally well.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Visually captivating, the camera is more scathing than the screenplay. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Amparo Cabal

reviews.text: The Menu is the most entertaining ensemble film since Knives Out, and the most engaging horror-satire since Get Out. But no matter what comparisons and assumptions are made, The Menu will not be the movie you expect.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: The more ridiculous and severe the courses and their supplements become, the more original and hilarious it all is.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: It's black comedy at its most zesty.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A deliciously dark black comedy with sharp social commentary and a brilliant ensemble cast, it's a delectably nasty treat that leaves a lasting impact.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: THE MENU is a twisted little horror satire, in which form and content harmonize wonderfully and Ralph Fiennes, as chef and storyteller at the same time, is preparing a really entertaining, if not completely filling meal for us.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: The Menu combines a wicked mix of culinary porn, horror elements and pitch-black comedy all beautifully wrapped in a well-paced 106-minute length.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: The Menu keeps you on your toes while offering more than just your basic thrilling confection.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: Deviously manipulative, like a highbrow Saw.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: A delightfully sharp comedy that never over-plays it's jokes.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: The Menu is deliciously twisted as it takes jabs at the restaurant industry and foodie culture. Ralph Fiennes is intense yet hilarious as the deranged chef and Anya Taylor-Joy continues to impress. The biggest and most laughs I've had in a movie all year.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: At its best, The Menu feels like Clue with more perfectly plated bone marrow. Do they give Michelin stars for movies?
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: The audience is immersed in a culinary experience that is masterfully crafted by Chef Slowik and his eerily obedient line of cooks. Even as the comedic horror takes its twists and turns, The Menu stays true to one thing: the art of fine dining.
reviews.author: Christine Nbemeneh

reviews.text: The film’s contempt for arrogance and entitlement is straightforward and satisfying, but when other motives start driving the story... the revenge story curdles a bit.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: The Menu’s delicate dance of violence, comedy and artful staging combine to make it one of the most satisfying films of the year.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: As nasty as it is hilarious.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: The Menu is the ultimately middle finger to snobbery and modern social dynamics, told in a delightfully intense, hilarious way.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: Mark Mylod’s high-stakes nerve-fryer couples darkness with honesty and marinades it in quality comedy. Ralph Fiennes is killer-good!
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: With excellent performances, witty writing, and confident direction all around, you’re going to want to order off The Menu.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: Sharp, cruel, and cathartic, The Menu is sublime.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: It’s playful and thought-provoking in all the right ways, and holds up a mirror to society’s increasingly superficial consumption of art. Mylod has proven himself to be an extremely versatile filmmaker, and The Menu is all the evidence you need.
reviews.author: Wilson Kwong

reviews.text: There’s no politics here, just a desire to follow the tide of public opinion right into their wallets, yet I can’t blame anyone for wanting to just go with the flow.
reviews.author: C.J. Prince

reviews.text: ...it only succeeds in making you wish there were something meatier to chew on...
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: The Menu provides unnerving satirical commentary on the class divide and how the wealthy are a bottomless pit of need that will never be satisfied.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: Everything on the menu of “The Menu” looks good enough, but once its moldy tirade against the one percent has been fully dished out, it’s plain to see there’s not a whole lot of meat on the bone here.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: At the risk of sounding hokey: it's a new spin on a familiar flavor, like pickle ice cream or a chocolate hamburger. The Menu lands its joke about the Chef Table-ification of cuisine while also finding nuance in its “capitalism is a plague” messaging.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: While this satirical thriller is never short on tensions, The Menu is a highly entertaining and hysterical experience to savor and relish.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Delivers its messaging in a highly entertaining manner, with well-observed dialogue, and some exquisite performances, especially from Hong Chau and Anya Taylor-Joy. It’s nihilistic, world-burning feel is as caustic as expected from Succession's writers.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: The Menu serves a delicious meal of murder, laughs, and commentary on class warfare and consumerism, with a stellar cast led by a commanding Ralph Fiennes.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: The Menu is a savory, satisfying whodunit with magnificent performances from Anna Taylor-Joy and Ralph Fiennes - who leave you wanting and yearning for more
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: A black-hearted, mini-masterpiece
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: All the actors are fun, but the two lead actors (sorry, I can’t resist) are so good they’re delicious.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: With these top notch performances, a smartly written script, and a ghastly series of events, The Menu is sure to set itself apart as one of the most entertaining films of this season…
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: The Menu has tasty treats but leaves you a bit hungry for more.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: “The Menu” is made with a love for satisfying storytelling. Impassioned direction, a tremendous cast, and outstanding technical prowess are the garnish sprinkled over layered themes at the core.
reviews.author: Nadia Dalimonte

reviews.text: I’m not 100% convinced this film has as much to say about high society as it thinks it does, and yet it’s an undeniably fun flick, a movie with almost no heroes.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Audiences may not have much of an appetite after watching the film, but the experience, like Slowik’s promise, will be one they won’t soon forget.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: While the sophisticated and dry horror-comedy tantalizes with a feast for the senses and a compelling ensemble cast, The Menu‘s satire lacks bite.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: [Fiennes'] performance is in perfect harmony with Mylod’s direction: Both are defined by a rigid, meticulous, luxurious style that masks a wellspring of bitterness, disgust and rage.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: A vengeful dark comedy that probes percolating class anxieties.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: The Menu might not nail some of the more substantial courses but it’ll do as a light snack.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: The Menu is a savage commentary on our materialistic consumerist tendencies, but surprisingly it is also a tale of reclaiming passion for who you are and what you do. Consider me well-fed, and expect me to return for seconds.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: Ralph Fiennes Serves Up A Delightfully Wicked Feast.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Alas, even with promising ingredients that have been assembled, this tepid thriller is one that grows increasingly tiresome with each course.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: “The Menu” does do one thing exceptionally well: it holds your attention and makes you think for a time that any outcome is possible. That alone is something to salivate over.
reviews.author: Christian Blauvelt

synopsis: A couple (Anya Taylor-Joy and Nicholas Hoult) travels to a coastal island to eat at an exclusive restaurant where the chef (Ralph Fiennes) has prepared a lavish menu, with some shocking surprises.
